summary: Add customer_note column idempotently, backfill existing notes, deploy new app with faked migration to avoid duplicate column error, then drop note column after old app retired.
write_consistency: During expand both columns coexist; old app writes to note, new app writes to customer_note. Backfill copies note values to customer_note. After deploy_new, new app is primary writer of customer_note; old app continues writing note until retire_old removes note column. Most recent write from either version is visible via the coexisting columns, ensuring no data loss.
revision_notes: Root cause: The expand_column SQL stage added customer_note via ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, but deploy_new's Django migration (migration: apply) re-attempted AddField for the same column, causing ProgrammingError: column already exists. Since the new app's migration is state-only and issues no SQL, the migration must be faked (migration: fake) to mark it applied without executing SQL, avoiding the conflict.

stages.description: Add the new customer_note column idempotently so both old and new code can operate concurrently.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note so reads from the new version see the same data.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Deploy the new-staged Saleor version; its Django model now references customer_note. The migration is faked (migration: fake) so Django does not re-add the already-existing column, avoiding the conflict.
Remove the old note column once the new app is confirmed to be handling all writes and reads.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;

stages.description: Retire the old version of Saleor that only knows the note column. After this stage the note column is gone and only customer_note remains in the schema.
